data.name: Athirappilly
data.description: Athirappilly Falls, often referred to as the "Niagara Falls of India," is a breath-taking waterfall located in the Thrissur district, which is approximately 30 kilometers from Chalakudy. This majestic cascade, surrounded by lush green forests, is a popular tourist destination. Multiple viewpoints offer visitors stunning panoramic views of the waterfall. Visitors can also explore the well-maintained trekking trails that lead to the base of the falls, offering stunning views of the waterfall and the surrounding landscape. The area is home to a variety of wildlife, including elephants, monkeys, and diverse bird species. The Forest Department offers trekking and sightseeing packages in Athirappilly as part of the ecotourism program.

data.name: Peechi - Vazhani
data.description: Peechi-Vazhani Wildlife Sanctuary is a haven for nature lovers, offering a serene and picturesque escape. Located in the Thrissur district, it is home to diverse flora and fauna, making it a popular destination for birdwatchers, wildlife enthusiasts, and adventure seekers. The sanctuary boasts lush green forests, serene lakes, and breath-taking landscapes. Visitors can enjoy trekking, hiking, and coracle rides offered by the Kerala Forest Department.

data.name: Chimmony
data.description: Chimmony Wildlife Sanctuary, nestled in the Western Ghats of Thrissur district is a hidden gem for nature lovers. This pristine sanctuary boasts lush tropical rainforests, cascading waterfalls, and diverse wildlife, making it a perfect destination for trekking, birdwatching, and wildlife spotting. The sanctuary is home to dense evergreen and semi-evergreen forests, providing a habitat for a variety of flora and fauna. Visitors can enjoy trekking, cycling, turtle ride, offered by the Kerala Forest Department.

data.name: Vazhachal
data.description: Vazhachal and Athirappally, nestled in the Western Ghats, and located in Thrissur District, offer a breath-taking experience for nature lovers and adventure enthusiasts. Together, they form a captivating ecotourism destination, renowned for lush greenery, cascading waterfalls, and diverse wildlife. Athirappally Falls, often called the "Niagara of India," is a breathtaking sight, with its powerful cascade of water, whereas Vazhachal offers a serene and picturesque setting, with its cascading waterfalls, dense forests, and tranquil streams. The Forest Department offers trekking and sightseeing packages for visitors.

data.name: Chulannur
data.description:
Chulanoor Peafowl Sanctuary: Where the Peacocks Dance
Nestled amidst the serene landscapes of Palakkad district in Kerala, the Chulanoor Peafowl Sanctuary, locally known as "Mayiladumpara" (the rock where peacocks dance), is a captivating haven for India's national bird. This unique sanctuary, established in 2007 and dedicated to the memory of renowned ornithologist K.K. Neelakantan, offers an unparalleled opportunity to witness the majestic Indian Peafowl in its natural habitat.......
Spread across approximately 3.42 square kilometers of dry deciduous forests and scrubland, Chulanoor provides an ideal environment for peafowls to thrive. Early mornings and late afternoons are the best times to visit, when the male peacocks often display their spectacular iridescent plumage and perform their elaborate courtship dances – a truly mesmerizing sight for photographers and nature enthusiasts alike.
